summary: Adversarial testing of the FR-3 balanced-brace JSDoc guard against 10 boundary, failure-path, and regression scenarios. Initial run revealed one bypass: the guard's STRAY_BLOCK detection only inspected the first non-space character after the balanced type region, missing orphaned {} blocks embedded in descriptive prose (scenario 3: `@returns {string} the result is {}`). The guard was fixed in the same commit to scan the entire rest of the line for any `{` character after the type region. Post-fix run: 10/10 scenarios pass, all 4 existing fixtures (malformed-1/2/3 + clean-1) still produce expected results, and production scope (apps/ packages/ convex/, 663 typed tags) still returns 0 violations / exit 0. The fix is a minimal 7-line change to the awk scanner (lines 172-185 of check-jsdoc-balanced-braces.sh) that replaces the single-position check with a full-line scan from type_end+1 to len.

bypass_found.root_cause: The guard's STRAY_BLOCK detection (Rule 3) used `next_pos = type_end + 1` and only checked the first non-space character after the balanced type. When descriptive prose intervenes between the type and the orphaned {}, the guard never reaches the stray block.
bypass_found.fix: Replaced the single-position check with a full-line scan from type_end+1 to len. If any `{` is found at any position after the balanced type, flag as STRAY_BLOCK. This matches the spec's intent: 'depth goes back up from 0' at any point on the same line means a stray block.

evidence.description: Multi-line @param — type split across two lines: `@param {Map<string,` on line 4, `number>}` on line 5.
evidence.initial_run: PASS — guard correctly detects depth never returns to 0 on the first line

evidence.description: Multi-line @returns — type split across two lines: `@returns {Promise<` on line 4, `string | null>}` on line 5.
evidence.initial_run: PASS — guard correctly detects depth never returns to 0 on the first line

evidence.description: Orphaned {} block after prose: `@returns {string} the result is {}` — type is balanced, but `{}` appears at the end of the line after descriptive text.
evidence.guard_output_initial: PASS: All 1 typed @param/@returns tags ... have balanced braces.
evidence.guard_output_post_fix: FAIL: 1 malformed @param/@returns tag(s) ... STRAY_BLOCK — * @returns {string} the result is {}

evidence.description: Backtick template literal inside @param type: `@param {(x: string) => `hello ${x}`}`. The guard treats `${x}` as a balanced inner block.
evidence.initial_run: PASS — guard sees depth=0 after outer closing brace, reports balanced
evidence.documentation_note: Backticks are not JSDoc-spec-valid in type expressions, but the guard checks syntactic brace balance, not JSDoc-spec validity. This is a documented limitation of the syntactic invariant approach.

evidence.description: JSDoc-style comment inside a brace region: `@param {{ /** a:b */ a: string; b: number }} row` — all braces balance.
Trailing semicolon in object type: `@param {{ a: string; b: number; }} opts` — legal in JSDoc/TS.
TypeScript generic with default: `@param {Map<string, T = string>}` — `=` inside angle brackets is a TS default.
Nested generics: `@returns {Promise<ReturnType<typeof fetch>>}` — deeply nested angle brackets, no stray braces.
Union of two function types: `@param {((x: number) => string) | ((x: string) => string)}` — all braces and parens balance.

regression_checks.check: Production scope (apps/ packages/ convex/) still clean

handoff: Adversarial testing complete. The FR-3 guard has been hardened against the embedded-{} in prose bypass (scenario 3). The fix is a minimal 7-line change that scans the full remainder of each @param/@returns line for any `{` character after the balanced type region. All 10 adversarial scenarios pass. All 4 existing fixtures still produce expected results. Production scope (663 typed tags, 2237 files) still returns 0 violations / exit 0. The fix preserves the syntactic invariant approach (no regex matching, no symbol-name grep) consistent with FR-20. Final acceptance should verify: (1) the adversarial runner exits 0, (2) the guard's production scope still exits 0, (3) the 4 existing fixtures still produce their expected exit codes, and (4) the guard's Rule 3 comment now documents the full-line scan behaviour.
